interface.signature: int n, List[List[int]] edges, int start -> int

preconditions.description: The number of nodes is between 2 and 3000 inclusive.
The number of edges is between 1 and the maximum possible for a graph with n nodes.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and 0 <= w <= 10**5 for [u, v, w] in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two nodes within the valid range, and the weight is non-negative and ≤ 10^5.
The starting node is within the valid range of node numbers.

postconditions.expression: return_value == sum(w for [u, v, w] in selected_edges)
postconditions.description: The returned value is the sum of the weights of the edges in the minimum spanning tree (MST) constructed using Prim's algorithm starting from the given node.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for [u, v, w] in selected_edges)
postconditions.description: All edges in the selected MST connect nodes within the valid range.
The MST contains exactly n-1 edges, where n is the number of nodes.

postconditions.expression: all(connected(u, v, selected_edges) for u in range(1, n + 1) for v in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The MST connects all nodes, meaning there is a path between any two nodes in the subgraph.
The MST has no cycles, meaning there is exactly one path between any two nodes.

postconditions.expression: return_value == min(total_weight for total_weight in possible_mst_weights(edges, n, start))
postconditions.description: The returned value is the minimum possible total weight among all valid MSTs starting from the given node.
